story: The patient is a 53-year-old man with type 2 diabetes. The note does not mention when he was diagnosed. He has taken metformin 1000 mg twice daily for about 6 months and tolerates it well, with no GI upset, intolerance, or contraindication. The note describes him as adherent. His HbA1c was 8.4% (drawn 11/03/2022), creatinine was within normal limits, and home fasting glucose runs mostly 160s-190s. BMI is 33.6. The note records no personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2, no pancreatitis history, and no current GLP-1 agent. On 2022-12-06, the endocrinologist requests an Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, added to continued metformin at the same dose.

This 31-year-old woman has type 2 diabetes mellitus and is overweight. The note does not mention when she was diagnosed. She has taken metformin for about 9 months with good reported adherence and no significant GI upset or other adverse effects. The note does not mention the metformin dose. She has never been on a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Her HbA1c on 07/05/2022 was 9.3%, home fasting glucose values are often in the 160s-190s mg/dL, and her BMI is 32.0 kg/m². She denies hypoglycemia, polyuria, polydipsia, or visual changes and has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. On 2022-08-02, the endocrinologist requested Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, to be added to continued metformin.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman whose chart diagnosis is prediabetes. The note states she does not carry a documented diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and does not mention when her glycemic problems were first identified. She has taken metformin, currently 1000 mg twice daily, for about 8 months. She tolerates it well with no GI upset or other adverse effects, reports good adherence, has reduced refined carbohydrates, and walks three to four times weekly. Her HbA1c was 8.5% on 10/07/2022. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or weight changes, and her BMI is 31.2. The endocrinologist is requesting Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen in addition to continued metformin. The note does not mention a starting dose or titration plan.

A 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes was seen for a Family Medicine follow-up on 7/17/22. The note does not mention when her diabetes was diagnosed. She has taken metformin since March 2022 (about 4 months, ongoing), currently 1000mg BID, daily and well tolerated, with no GI upset, intolerance, or contraindication noted. She reports diet efforts and walking 3x/wk. Her HbA1c was 7.1% on 6/25/22, described as not at goal. Her BMI is 33.9, and she also has HTN and hyperlipidemia. The note records no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2, no pancreatitis history, and no current GLP-1 agent. The prescriber requests the Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, to be added to continued metformin.

The patient is a 74-year-old male with type 2 diabetes. The note documents the diagnosis but does not mention when it was made. He has taken metformin, currently 1000mg BID, for about 6 months, tolerating it well with no GI complaints, intolerance, or contraindication, and he reports adherence. He is not taking any other GLP-1 agent, and the note records no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. His HbA1c was 9.4% (drawn 4/11/22), and his home fasting readings run mostly 180s-220s, without hypoglycemia, polyuria, or polydipsia. BMI is 31.3. On 2022-05-13 the endocrinologist requested Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL pen SC weekly, to be added to continued metformin.

The patient is a 51-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, and the note does not mention when she was diagnosed. She has taken metformin 1000 mg twice daily for about 9 months, tolerating it well with no gastrointestinal upset or other adverse effects. She reports good adherence, dietary changes, and walking three to four times weekly. Her HbA1c was 8.6% on 08/13/2023, with fasting home readings mostly in the 160s to 190s. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, hypoglycemia, and pancreatitis history, and has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. Her BMI is 33.9, and she takes no GLP-1 agent. On 2023-09-02, Endocrinology requested Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, to be added to continued metformin.

This 24-year-old woman has type 2 diabetes mellitus; the note does not mention when she was diagnosed. She started metformin in March 2023 and has taken it for about 4 months, now 1000 mg twice daily, with good adherence and no GI upset, diarrhea, or other adverse effects. She is not on any GLP-1 receptor agonist. Her HbA1c drawn 2023-06-29 was 9.5%, which the note calls well above her individualized goal. Her BMI is 34.6. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or hypoglycemia, and has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. On 2023-07-10, Endocrinology requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen once weekly, added to metformin.

This 60-year-old woman has type 2 diabetes mellitus, though the note does not mention when she was diagnosed. She has taken metformin 1000 mg twice daily for about 6 months with good adherence, alongside ongoing dietary efforts. She has had no GI upset, diarrhea, or other adverse effects. No other diabetes medicines are listed, and she is not on any GLP-1 receptor agonist. Her HbA1c was 7.0% on 07/16/2023, above her individualized goal. Renal function is within normal limits, and her BMI is 33.9. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or hypoglycemia, and has no personal or family history of MTC, MEN2, or pancreatitis. On 2023-07-23, her endocrinologist requests adding Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen once weekly to continued metformin.

This 37-year-old female has prediabetes, per the note, with no established diagnosis of type 2 diabetes. The note does not mention when her glycemic abnormalities began. Management so far has been dietary changes and walking three to four times weekly, for a duration the note does not mention. She has never taken metformin, which the note states is contraindicated because of stage 4 chronic kidney disease, and has never used a GLP-1 receptor agonist. On 2023-03-27, her HbA1c was 6.8% and eGFR 27 mL/min/1.73 m². BMI is 34.5, and she denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or weight loss. The family medicine prescriber requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, titrated to 1 mg weekly.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus; the note does not mention when she was diagnosed. She has been managed with diet and walking most days, for a duration the note does not state, and the note lists no prior or current diabetes medicines. She has never taken metformin, which the note describes as contraindicated because of stage 4 chronic kidney disease, with eGFR consistently below 30 mL/min/1.73 m². Her HbA1c was 9.0% and eGFR 27 mL/min/1.73 m², both on 01/23/2023. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, or hypoglycemia, and reports no personal or family history of MTC or MEN2 and no pancreatitis. Endocrinology requests Trulicity 1.5 mg/0.5 mL pen, once weekly, on 2023-03-03.

This 17-year-old female is followed in endocrinology for prediabetes and insulin resistance, with obesity (BMI 37.1 kg/m²) and acanthosis nigricans. The note states type 2 diabetes has not been diagnosed. She has taken metformin for about 9 months with good adherence and no adverse effects, though the note does not mention the dose. She has also reduced sugar-sweetened beverages, walks several days weekly, and has never used a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Her most recent HbA1c was 8.0% on 10/03/2023, a single unconfirmed value, and repeat HbA1c and fasting glucose are planned. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or weight loss and has no MTC, MEN2, or pancreatitis history. The prescriber requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen.

The patient is a 31-year-old male with type 2 diabetes; the note does not mention when it was diagnosed. He started metformin in March 2023 and has taken it for about 8 months with good adherence and no GI upset, diarrhea, or other adverse effects. The note does not mention the dose. His HbA1c on 10/27/2023 was 7.5%, described as above his individualized goal. He denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or symptomatic hypoglycemia. The note records no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 and no past GLP-1 receptor agonist use. On 2023-11-13, the Family Medicine prescriber requested Trulicity 1.5 mg/0.5 mL pen once weekly, to be added to continued metformin.

This is a 46-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus, along with hyperlipidemia and overweight; the note does not mention when the diabetes was diagnosed. He has taken metformin 1000 mg twice daily for about 3 months, since January 2023, with good adherence and no GI upset or other adverse effects, and he is not on another GLP-1 receptor agonist. His HbA1c on 04/19/2023 was 8.3%, with home fasting readings mostly in the 150s to 180s mg/dL. His BMI is 30.7 kg/m², and he denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or symptomatic hypoglycemia. The note records no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. On 2023-04-27, the endocrinologist requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen once weekly, added to continued metformin.

A 56-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, along with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; the note does not mention when the diabetes was diagnosed. She has taken metformin 1000 mg twice daily for about 9 months with good adherence and no gastrointestinal upset or other adverse effects, alongside a carbohydrate-conscious diet and walking three to four times weekly. Her HbA1c was 7.3% (drawn 09/01/2023), BMI is 33.1, renal function is preserved, and she denies hyperglycemic symptoms or hypoglycemia. The note stresses no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 and no current GLP-1 agent. The endocrinologist requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, added to metformin.

A 61-year-old male, as stated in the note, was evaluated for type 2 diabetes earlier this year, and the note does not mention a diagnosis-time HbA1c. He has taken metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals for about 2 months, consistently and with good tolerance, and the note reports no GI upset or other adverse effects. He has also cut refined carbohydrates and sugary beverages and walks about 20 minutes most days. His HbA1c drawn 2023-04-06 was 6.8%, and his BMP was within normal limits. His BMI is 31.8, and he denies hyperglycemic or hypoglycemic symptoms. He has no personal or family history of MTC or MEN2. The endocrinologist is requesting Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, added to metformin, on 2023-04-14.

The patient is a 79-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus; the note does not mention when she was diagnosed. She started metformin in March 2023 and has taken 1000 mg twice daily for about 9 months. She tolerates it well, without gastrointestinal upset, and reports good adherence. The note does not mention other diabetes medicines tried, and she takes no GLP-1 receptor agonist. Her HbA1c was 9.2% on 2023-11-16, her basic metabolic panel was normal, and her BMI is 30.6 kg/m². She reports occasional fatigue. The note stresses no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. The endocrinologist requests Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL weekly, added to metformin.

This 65-year-old male has type 2 diabetes, with the date of diagnosis not given in the note, alongside hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been on metformin for about 6 months (started Apr 2023, ongoing), currently 1000mg BID, taken as directed and tolerated well with no GI complaints, intolerance, or contraindication. The note does not mention an A1c or any other recent labs. He denies polyuria, polydipsia, hypoglycemia symptoms, and vision changes. BMI is 31.2, BP 132/80, and the foot exam is unremarkable. The note states he takes no other GLP-1 RA and has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2. The endocrinologist is requesting Trulicity 1.5 mg/0.5 mL pen SC once weekly, added to continued metformin.

The patient is a 29-year-old listed as male, with type 2 diabetes documented in the chart; the note does not mention when it was diagnosed. No diabetes medicine is currently taken, metformin has never been tried, and the note records no intolerance or contraindication to it; the patient is not on another GLP-1 agent. HbA1c was 8.0% (drawn 01/25/2024), described as above goal, with mild fatigue and polyuria for a few weeks, weight 241 lb, and BMI 34.6. Metformin was discussed as first line, but the patient prefers a GLP-1 for weight benefit. Family Medicine requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen on 2024-03-03, planning to start and titrate per label.

The patient is a 43-year-old nonbinary adult (they/them) with type 2 diabetes. The note says the diagnosis is documented in the chart but gives no diagnosis date. They take metformin 1000mg BID, tolerated well with no GI upset, intolerance, or contraindication, though the note does not mention how long they have been on it. They have never started a GLP-1 RA. HbA1c was 8.7% (drawn 04/26/2024), with home fasting sugars of 160s-190s, no hypoglycemia, eGFR wnl, and BMI 34.1. On 2024-06-05, the endocrinologist is requesting Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL pen, SC weekly, added to continued metformin.

The patient is an 86-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, described as a long history; the note does not give a diagnosis date. He takes metformin and tolerates it well, with no GI complaints or intolerance. The note does not mention the dose or how long he has taken it. He is not on any other GLP-1 agent. The note does not mention an A1c or any recent labs. He denies hypoglycemia symptoms, weighs 84.1 kg, and has decreased monofilament sensation at the left great toe. The chart documents a personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma/MEN2, and the boxed warning was discussed. Endocrinology requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen on 2024-11-30.

The patient is a 33-year-old female. The note does not state a diabetes diagnosis, when it began, or its duration. On management, the note lists only cetirizine 10mg as needed and a daily multivitamin. It states she has never tried metformin and is not currently taking any other GLP-1 RA, and it does not mention any prior diabetes medicines or tolerability. At the 6/8/24 endocrinology follow-up, her most recent HbA1c was 7.0%, drawn 5/21/24, with other results described as unremarkable. She reported feeling okay with no new complaints, and the exam was unremarkable. She has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2 and no pancreatitis history. The endocrinology prescriber requests Trulicity 1.5 mg/0.5 mL pen, injected subcutaneously once weekly.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The note does not mention when he was diagnosed. He has been managed with diet and increased physical activity, for a duration the note does not mention. Metformin has never been tried, with no known intolerance or contraindication, and he takes no glucose-lowering medication. His HbA1c was 7.1% (drawn 02/16/2024), which the note describes as above goal. He reports occasional polydipsia, and the exam notes a BMI of 31.4 kg/m² and mild acanthosis nigricans. He has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2. The endocrinologist requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, dated 2024-03-01, to start therapy.

A 36-year-old male has a documented diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus and is overweight. The note does not mention when he was diagnosed. He has taken metformin for about 9 months with good adherence and no gastrointestinal upset or other adverse effects, though the note does not mention the dose. His most recent HbA1c, drawn 09/22/2024, was 6.8%, above an individualized target of below 6.5%. Weight is 214 lb and BMI 30.7 kg/m². He denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or symptomatic hypoglycemia. He has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 and takes no GLP-1 receptor agonist. On 2024-10-02, his endocrinologist requested Trulicity 1.5 mg/0.5 mL pen once weekly as add-on therapy to metformin.

A 63-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia; the note does not mention when the diabetes was diagnosed. She started metformin around February 2025, reached 1000 mg twice daily by April 2025, and has taken it for about 9 months with no GI upset or other adverse effects and good reported adherence. She has also reduced refined carbohydrates and sugary beverages and walks 3 to 4 times weekly. Her most recent HbA1c was 7.7% on 09/25/2025, and her BMI is 32.4. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision or hypoglycemia, has no personal or family history of MTC or MEN2, and takes no GLP-1 receptor agonist. The endocrinologist requests Trulicity 1.5 mg/0.5 mL pen once weekly, added to continued metformin.

An 85-year-old man has long-standing type 2 diabetes; the note does not give a diagnosis date. He was on metformin, which he stopped himself because of persistent diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and nausea, and the note says he is not able to retry it. The note does not say how long he took metformin or at what dose, and lists no other diabetes medicines. His HbA1c was 7.2% on 2/26/2025, his BMP is within normal limits, and his creatinine is stable. The note highlights mild decreased monofilament sensation in both feet, no hypoglycemia, a BMI of 27.4, and no history of thyroid cancer, MEN2, or pancreatitis. The endocrinologist requests Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL weekly.

The patient is a 51-year-old female with type 2 diabetes documented in the chart; the note does not mention when the diabetes was diagnosed. The patient is a 36-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and overweight. The note does not mention when the diabetes was diagnosed. The endocrinologist requests Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL pen once weekly, added to metformin.

A 44-year-old man with type 2 diabetes (the note does not mention when he was diagnosed) was seen in endocrinology follow-up on 11/05/25. He has taken metformin 1000mg BID for about 12 months, tolerating it well with no GI upset, and has had no prior GLP-1 trial. He reports home fingerstick glucose still running above goal despite adherence, with no hypoglycemia symptoms, polyuria, polydipsia, or vision changes. The note does not mention an A1c or any other lab values. Weight is 231 lb, BMI 33.1, and BP 134/82. He has no history of medullary thyroid cancer, MEN2, or pancreatitis. The endocrinologist requests Ozempic 1 mg/dose pen, titrating semaglutide to 1 mg weekly alongside continued metformin.

A 47-year-old man has type 2 diabetes mellitus, along with controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia; the note does not mention when the diabetes was diagnosed. Endocrinology requests Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL once weekly, added to metformin.

The patient is a 20-year-old female (DOB 06/27/2005). The note does not mention a diabetes diagnosis, its type, or when it began. She has taken metformin daily for about 9 months, with good reported adherence and no GI upset, intolerance, or contraindication. No other diabetes medicines and no prior GLP-1 use are noted. The note does not mention any lab results, including A1c or glucose, or weight. At the 10/20/2025 visit, vitals were normal (BP 118/74) and the exam was unremarkable. ROS was negative for polyuria, polydipsia, and vision changes. She denied personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, MEN2, pancreatitis, or gallbladder issues. The Family Medicine prescriber requests Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL pen, SC once weekly, added to continued metformin.

The endocrinologist is requesting Mounjaro 5 mg/0.5 mL pen once weekly, added to continued metformin.

He has taken metformin for about 9 months with good tolerance and adherence, alongside diet and activity changes. The note does not mention the metformin dose. His most recent HbA1c is 6.3% (drawn 09/07/2025), and he denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, or weight change. The note does not mention weight or BMI.
